meta.title: Leonida Trophy Guide — all 55 GTA 6 trophies
meta.difficulty_note: No trophy asks for elite skill. The hard parts are the long grinds: 250 stunts, 42 gold Shooting Range challenges, 100 WAiNK spots and 100% completion. Everything else is patience and following the steps.
meta.time_note: Rough estimate for a first playthrough plus cleanup: about 60 to 80 hours of story and side strands, then 120 hours or so of activities, collectibles, robberies and miscellany. Skilled players who already know the map will be faster.
meta.playthroughs_note: One playthrough is enough if you meditate at the Chapter 1 spots as you go. There is no mission replay, so the one possibly missable trophy needs care during Chapter 1 (see the missable warnings below).
meta.online_note: No trophy needs GTA Online or any online mode. Every trophy is earned in the single-player story and free roam.
meta.cheats_note: Turning cheats on disables trophies, so leave them off until the platinum pops.
meta.about: This guide covers every one of GTA VI's 55 PlayStation 5 trophies with its official name, description and grade exactly as PlayStation publishes them, plus a guide in the author's own words for each one: what to do, where and how, when it can be missed, and which source each fact comes from. Names and descriptions are PlayStation's own words; everything else is written for this guide.
meta.how_to_use: Start on the Checklist tab, tick trophies off as you earn them, and open any trophy to read its guide, steps, tips and sources. The Roadmap tab lays out the order to earn them in. Spoilers are hidden by default: story trophy names and descriptions stay covered until you tick them earned. Your progress is saved in the browser and can be exported to a file and imported back.

roadmap.summary: Three stages. Stage 1 is the story: play Chapters 1 to 4 and the final mission, finish the character strands as they unlock, and meditate at the Chapter 1 spots while you are there. Stage 2 is activities and collectibles: stunts, the shooting range, races, fishing, cards, WAiNK spots and exploring Leonida. Stage 3 is robberies, miscellany and the 100% completion grind, then the platinum.

stages.title: Story first — play it, mop up as you go
stages.description: Play the story from Gone Fishing through the final mission. Finish each chapter as it comes, and take the side strands for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone as they unlock rather than leaving them all for later. Meet strangers and work their strands across Leonida. Most important: meditate at every Chapter 1 spot while you are still in Chapter 1, because there is no mission replay and this is the one trophy that may be missable.
stages.focus: Chapters 1 to 4, the final mission, the five character strands, the stranger strands, and the Chapter 1 meditation spots.

stages.title: Activities and collectibles
stages.description: With the story done, work through the activities: 250 stunts, gold medals in all 42 Shooting Range challenges, a Top Fun drone race win at every location, 20 different race wins, beating Cal at fishing, one arcade game, 50 challenges, and trying all 9 activity types. Alongside them, hunt the unique animal for Bret, complete 3 Collectible Card sets, WAiNK It at 100 locations, discover 100 vehicles and explore all 52 areas of Leonida.
stages.focus: Stunts, shooting range, races, fishing, arcade, challenges, hunting, cards, WAiNK spots, vehicles and exploration.

stages.title: Robberies, miscellany and the platinum
stages.description: Finish the robbery set: a jewelry store undetected, 5 bank vaults, an armored truck, and one illegal operation for each of the 9 gangs. Then clear the miscellany: partner stunts, Combat Focus, the VCIA departure, the Rhinos, the Ocean Beach cocktail, the showroom smash, bowling, the partnership moment, the 500 choices, the two unconfirmed oddities, the strange sighting, the melee drive-by, laundering $250,000, spending $100,000, all 8 garages and 10 Scooter Bros registrations. That leaves 100% completion, and then the platinum.
stages.focus: Robberies, partner and combat feats, odd one-offs, money goals, and 100% completion.

chapters.notes: The opening chapter. It holds the Gone Fishing opener, the Chapter 1 completion trophy, the Breakfast Run mission, and the meditation spots that matter for the one possibly missable trophy. Meditate at every spot you pass; do not assume you can come back to them later.
The story widens across Leonida. The Cartel Heist and Child's Play missions sit here, and the chapter completion trophy pops when the last Chapter 2 mission ends.
Vice City opens up properly. Headliners and the VCIA Takedown are the named mission trophies here, and the chapter trophy follows the final Chapter 3 mission.
The endgame of the story. Operation Savage Glory is the named mission trophy, the chapter trophy pops at the end of Chapter 4, and the final mission closes the story with a gold trophy.
Free roam after the story. This is where the long grinds live: activities, collectibles, robberies, exploration and the 100% completion push. Nothing here is missable, so take it at your own pace.

play_order: Play the story straight through, Chapters 1 to 4 and the final mission, and do the character strands as they unlock.
In Chapter 1, meditate at every meditation spot you pass. This is the only trophy that may be missable.
Meet strangers whenever their icon appears and work their strands; 8 strands complete the set.
After the story, clear the activities in batches: stunts and races first, then the shooting range, then fishing and the arcade.
Fold collectibles into your travel: cards, WAiNK spots, vehicles and map areas all count while you drive between jobs.
Do the robbery set in one sweep once you have good weapons and a fast getaway car.
Leave the money goals (laundering, spending, garages) for last, when cash is plentiful.
Finish 100% completion, then let the platinum pop.
missable_warnings: Positive Mental Attitude is the only trophy flagged as possibly missable: meditate at every spot across Leonida, and do the Chapter 1 spots during Chapter 1, because there is no mission replay. Whether it truly counts as missable is unconfirmed.
No other trophy in this list is missable. Every other trophy can be earned in free roam after the story, at any time.
Bad Luck, I Guess and Ten Pin are labelled unconfirmed: their exact triggers are not yet pinned down, so the guides below give the best current reading and say so plainly.
Cheats disable trophies. Keep them off until the platinum pops.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing to do for this one directly. Work the roadmap in order, keep the checklist honest, and it arrives on its own — most players get it right after the 100% completion trophy, A Long Road, since that is the last big grind. If it does not pop, check the checklist for the one trophy still unticked.
steps: Earn all 54 other trophies, following the roadmap stages in order.
Finish 100% completion for A Long Road, the usual last trophy before the platinum.
Check the checklist if the platinum does not pop: one trophy is still unticked.
tips: The platinum has no separate requirement beyond the other 54, so never grind for it directly.
Export your progress file before the final push, so a lost save cannot cost you the record.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy most players earn. Play through the intro as directed: follow the on-screen prompts, drive where the game tells you, and finish the mission's closing beat. It cannot be missed — it pops as soon as the mission completes, and it is the doorway into Chapter 1.
steps: Start a new game and follow the opening prompts into Gone Fishing.
Play the mission through to its closing beat.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
tips: Nothing here needs preparation; just play the opener.
If you are replaying the intro, the trophy pops again on completion.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1 and the trophy pops when the chapter closes. Chapter 1 is the shortest chapter, around 15 hours, and it sets up Lucia and Jason's story in Leonida. While you play it, meditate at every spot you pass — that feeds the one possibly missable trophy, Positive Mental Attitude — and meet any strangers whose icons appear.
steps: Play every Chapter 1 mission in order until the chapter closes.
Meditate at each meditation spot you pass along the way.
The trophy pops at the chapter's closing scene.
tips: Do not rush past the meditation spots; there is no mission replay.
Stranger icons that appear in Chapter 1 are worth stopping for.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 2 and the trophy pops when the chapter closes. Chapter 2 widens the map and the stakes, with The Cartel Heist and Child's Play among its named missions. Keep doing the character strands as they unlock — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each have a final mission with its own trophy — and keep an eye out for strangers.
steps: Play every Chapter 2 mission in order until the chapter closes.
Take the character strands as they unlock instead of leaving them all for later.
The trophy pops at the chapter's closing scene.
tips: Stock up on armour and ammo before the chapter's bigger shootouts.
Side strands done now save a long cleanup later.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 3 and the trophy pops when the chapter closes. Vice City proper opens up in this chapter, with Headliners and the VCIA Takedown among its named missions. By now you should have a good car, a full weapon wheel and a feel for the wanted system, because the chapter's set pieces lean on all three.
steps: Play every Chapter 3 mission in order until the chapter closes.
Keep a fast car and a stocked weapon wheel ready for the set pieces.
The trophy pops at the chapter's closing scene.
tips: Use the time between missions to grab collectibles you pass.
The VCIA Takedown is a good moment to practise losing the cops cleanly.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 4 and the trophy pops when the chapter closes. Chapter 4 is the story's endgame, and its missions are the toughest of the four chapters, so go in with full armour, upgraded weapons and a fast car. Operation Savage Glory is the named mission trophy here, and the final mission follows close behind it.
steps: Play every Chapter 4 mission in order until the chapter closes.
Stock full armour and ammo before the chapter's big shootouts.
The trophy pops at the chapter's closing scene.
tips: Save before the chapter's hardest missions so a failed attempt costs nothing.
Finish any character strands still open before the finale.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of the story and this gold trophy pops. It is the last story beat, so expect a long, multi-part mission with a big set piece at the end. Go in prepared: full armour, your best weapons, and a save from just before you start. Once it pops, the whole of Leonida opens up for free roam and the long cleanup begins.
steps: Finish Chapter 4 to unlock the final mission.
Stock full armour and your best weapons, then start it.
Play the mission through to its closing scene; the gold pops on completion.
tips: Save right before the final mission so you can retry cleanly.
After it pops, the post-game cleanup is all free roam — nothing is missable from here.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the Breakfast Run mission and the trophy pops. Breakfast Run is an early story mission, so it comes naturally as you play through the chapters — just follow the mission marker when it appears and play it to the end. There is no special requirement beyond finishing the mission itself.
steps: Follow the mission marker to start Breakfast Run.
Play the mission through to its closing beat.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
tips: Early missions teach the driving and shooting basics; take your time with them.
No preparation is needed for this one.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist mission and the trophy pops. This is one of the story's big heist set pieces, so expect a planned job with a loud finish: bring heavy weapons, full armour, and a fast getaway car parked close to the exit. Follow the crew's plan, then improvise when it goes sideways — it will.
steps: Reach The Cartel Heist in the story and start it.
Bring heavy weapons, full armour and a fast getaway car.
Finish the heist and escape; the trophy pops on completion.
tips: Park your getaway car facing the exit before the job starts.
Ammo runs low in long shootouts, so grab dropped weapons as you go.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the Child's Play mission and the trophy pops. It is a story mission, so it arrives in order as you play — follow the marker, play it through, and the trophy follows the mission's closing scene. No extra step is needed beyond finishing the mission itself.
steps: Follow the mission marker to start Child's Play.
Play the mission through to its closing beat.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
tips: Story missions cannot be missed; they unlock in order.
If a mission fails, retry it from the checkpoint — progress is kept.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the Headliners mission and the trophy pops. Headliners is a mid-story mission, so it unlocks in order as you play through the chapters. Follow the marker, play it to the end, and the trophy follows the closing scene. Like the other mission trophies, there is no hidden requirement — finishing the mission is the whole job.
steps: Follow the mission marker to start Headliners.
Play the mission through to its closing beat.
The trophy pops when the mission completes.
tips: Keep a save from before the mission in case a set piece goes wrong.
Mid-story missions start to test driving under pressure — keep a sturdy car handy.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the VCIA Takedown mission and the trophy pops. The mission takes you to Vice City International Airport, so expect tight driving, security to dodge or fight, and a getaway that rewards a fast car. Play it through to the closing beat and the trophy follows. It is also good practice for losing a wanted level cleanly, which the later partner trophies need.
steps: Follow the mission marker to start VCIA Takedown.
Bring a fast car and expect airport security.
Play the mission through; the trophy pops on completion.
tips: Learn the airport's exits before the getaway starts.
A wanted level here is normal — losing it is part of the mission's flow.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the Operation Savage Glory mission and the trophy pops. This is one of the late-story operations, so expect a heavy combat mission with a lot of enemies and a long firefight. Full armour, your best automatic weapon and plenty of ammo are the preparation; patience and cover are the tactic. Finish it and the trophy follows the closing scene.
steps: Reach Operation Savage Glory late in the story and start it.
Bring full armour, a strong automatic weapon and plenty of ammo.
Fight through to the closing beat; the trophy pops on completion.
tips: Use cover and move in short bursts; standing in the open ends runs.
Pick up enemy weapons when your ammo runs low.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion and this gold trophy pops. Completion counts story missions, side strands, activities, collectibles, robberies and exploration together, so it is really the sum of everything else in this guide. The in-game stats screen shows your percentage and what is still missing — check it often in the final stretch, and work the missing categories one at a time instead of wandering.
steps: Finish the story, all side strands and the activity set.
Open the stats screen and note which categories are still short of 100%.
Clear the missing categories one at a time until the counter reads 100%.
tips: The stats screen is your best friend in the final stretch — it names what is missing.
Do the longest grinds (stunts, range, WAiNK) before the short ones, so the end feels quick.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts and this silver trophy pops. A stunt is any showy driving feat the game registers — jumps, near misses, drifts, airtime and the like — and the counter keeps climbing across the whole game, so a lot of them happen by accident while you play. To finish the count deliberately, find a good jump spot, a fast car, and repeat the run: hit the ramp, land clean, and loop back for another go.
steps: Drive fast and showy from the start; the counter climbs as you play.
Find a jump or ramp you can repeat and loop it with a fast car.
Keep going until the counter reads 250.
tips: A stunt counts when the game flashes its name on screen — watch for the pop-up.
Landing clean matters; a crash after a big jump can lose the stunt.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try all 9 activity types once each and the trophy pops. The activities are the game's side pastimes — racing, fishing, the shooting range, drone races, the arcade, bowling, and the rest of the set — and one try at each is all it takes. You do not need to win or finish anything, just start each type once. The activity list in the pause menu shows which types you have tried.
steps: Open the activity list and note the 9 types.
Start one of each type — winning is not required.
The trophy pops when the ninth type is tried.
tips: Do this early: it teaches you every activity before the long grinds.
If a type is unclear, its icon on the map leads you to it.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges and this silver trophy pops. The range has 42 challenges across its weapon types, and each one needs a gold score — not just a pass. Learn each challenge's rhythm first with a bronze run, then push for gold: aim for the head and centre rings, reload during the lulls, and do not rush the timed ones. This is the hardest activity trophy, so leave it for when your shooting is sharp.
steps: Visit the Shooting Range and work through the 42 challenges.
Learn each challenge with a bronze run, then push for gold.
Gold all 42 and the trophy pops.
tips: Head and centre-ring hits score far more than body hits.
Reload during the quiet beats, never in the middle of a wave.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations and the trophy pops. Each location has its own course, and you only need one win at each — no gold times, no perfect runs. Learn a course with a slow first lap, then race it properly: cut the corners, keep the drone low through the gates, and save the boost for the straights. The map marks every race location once you have found it.
steps: Find the Top Fun drone race locations on the map (14 in all).
Win one race at each location.
The trophy pops when the fourteenth location is won.
tips: A slow sighting lap beats a fast crash: learn the gates first.
Keep the drone low through gates and save boost for straights.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races and the trophy pops. Different races means different events, not the same race 20 times — the game counts each distinct race you win once. Pick the short street races first, learn their corners, and use a car with good acceleration rather than top speed. The race list shows which ones you have already won, so you can tick them off in order.
steps: Open the race list and pick a short street race you have not won.
Win it, then move to the next unwon race.
The trophy pops on your twentieth different win.
tips: Acceleration beats top speed on twisty street circuits.
Short races are the fastest way to build the count.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge and the trophy pops. Cal is the fishing rival, and the challenge is a head-to-head catch: out-fish him within the time limit. Pick the right bait for the spot, cast where the fish are showing, and reel steadily — yanking the rod snaps the line. If you lose, challenge him again; there is no penalty for retrying.
steps: Find Cal and start a fishing challenge.
Pick bait for the spot and cast where fish are showing.
Out-catch Cal before time runs out; retry if you lose.
tips: Reel steadily — yanking snaps the line and loses the fish.
Watch the water for where the fish are showing before you cast.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game and the trophy pops. Find an arcade machine in the world, pick any game on it, and play it through to its end — a high score is not needed, just a finished game. The arcade games are short, so this is one of the quickest trophies in the set, and a good palate cleanser between the long grinds.
steps: Find an arcade machine in the world.
Pick any game and play it through to the end.
The trophy pops when the game completes.
tips: Any game on the machine counts — pick the one you enjoy most.
A finished game is all it takes; no high score is needed.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Andy's strand and the trophy pops. Andy's missions unlock as you play the story — take them when his icon appears rather than leaving the whole strand for the end. The final mission is the strand's closing beat, so expect it to be longer than the earlier ones. Finish it and the trophy follows.
steps: Take Andy's missions as his icon appears during the story.
Work the strand through to its final mission.
Complete the final mission; the trophy pops.
tips: Character strands unlock in story order — do not skip the early ones.
The final mission is the longest of the strand, so go in prepared.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Kenton's strand and the trophy pops. Kenton's missions involve boats and the water around Leonida, so keep a boat handy and expect at least one chase on the water. Work the strand as it unlocks, and the final mission closes it out with a trophy.
steps: Take Kenton's missions as his icon appears during the story.
Work the strand through to its final mission.
Complete the final mission; the trophy pops.
tips: Keep a fast boat nearby for Kenton's water missions.
Boat chases reward smooth steering over top speed.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Billy's strand and the trophy pops. Billy's missions are solo rides and runs across Leonida, so keep a good bike or fast car ready. Take his missions as they unlock during the story and the strand closes with its final mission and this trophy.
steps: Take Billy's missions as his icon appears during the story.
Work the strand through to its final mission.
Complete the final mission; the trophy pops.
tips: A fast bike suits Billy's missions better than a car.
Solo rides are a good time to grab collectibles you pass.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida and this silver trophy pops. Strangers appear as icons on the map — stop and meet them whenever you see one, because their strands are short chains of missions that only unlock by talking to them. Eight completed strands is the count, and there are more than 8 strangers in the state, so you can skip any strand you dislike.
steps: Stop at stranger icons whenever they appear on the map.
Work each stranger's strand through to its end.
The trophy pops when the eighth strand completes.
tips: There are more than 8 strangers, so skip any strand you dislike.
Strands unlock by talking to the stranger — the icon is the trigger.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Randy's strand and the trophy pops. Randy's missions are supply runs — pickups, deliveries and the occasional ambush — so keep a sturdy vehicle with room for cargo and expect trouble on the road. Work the strand as it unlocks and the final mission closes it with this trophy.
steps: Take Randy's missions as his icon appears during the story.
Work the strand through to its final mission.
Complete the final mission; the trophy pops.
tips: A sturdy vehicle with cargo room suits Randy's runs.
Expect ambushes on deliveries; keep a weapon in reach.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Tyrone's strand and the trophy pops. Tyrone's missions lean on driving and music-scene jobs around Vice City, so keep a fast car ready and follow his markers. Take the missions as they unlock during the story and the strand's final mission closes it out.
steps: Take Tyrone's missions as his icon appears during the story.
Work the strand through to its final mission.
Complete the final mission; the trophy pops.
tips: A fast car suits Tyrone's driving-heavy missions.
Do the strand as it unlocks; the final mission is the longest.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.missable_note: Potentially missable: the Chapter 1 spots should be done during Chapter 1, because there is no mission replay. Whether it truly counts as missable is unconfirmed.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida and the trophy pops. Meditation spots are quiet places marked in the world — a balcony in Chapter 1 is the one to watch, because it is the spot most likely to be missable. Sit at each spot and meditate through the prompt; the game counts the spot once the meditation completes. Do the Chapter 1 spots during Chapter 1, and work the rest as you travel the map in free roam.
steps: In Chapter 1, meditate at every spot you pass, including the balcony spot.
After the story, visit the remaining meditation spots across Leonida.
The trophy pops when the eighteenth spot is meditated at.
tips: This is the only trophy flagged as possibly missable — do Chapter 1 spots in Chapter 1.
A spot counts only when the meditation completes, so stay seated until the prompt ends.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal for Bret and the trophy pops. Bret's hunt is a tracking job: follow the clues and tracks the mission gives you, move quietly, and take the shot when the animal is in range. A scoped rifle helps, and patience matters more than firepower — spooking the animal costs you the stalk. Finish the hunt and deliver the result to Bret.
steps: Take Bret's hunt and follow the tracks and clues.
Move quietly and wait for a clear shot at the unique animal.
Take the animal down and report back to Bret.
tips: A scoped rifle is the right tool; do not rush the shot.
Spooking the animal costs the stalk, so move slowly and stay downwind.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 Collectible Card sets and this silver trophy pops. Cards are hidden around Leonida in shops, houses and odd corners, and a set is complete when you hold every card in it. Pick up every card you pass while travelling — they add up fast — and use a card map for the last few stragglers of each set. Three finished sets is the count, and there are more sets than that in the game.
steps: Pick up every collectible card you pass while travelling.
Track which sets are close to complete in the collection menu.
Use a card map for the last few cards of three sets.
tips: Cards are small and easy to walk past — check shelves and counters.
Finish the sets with the fewest cards missing first.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations and this silver trophy pops. WAiNK spots are marked places around Leonida where you can do the WAiNK interaction, and each one counts once. They are spread across the whole map, so fold them into your travel: whenever you are near a marked spot, stop and do it. A WAiNK map helps for the last twenty or so, when the remaining spots are the ones you never happened to pass.
steps: Stop at every WAiNK spot you pass and do the interaction.
Fold WAiNK spots into your travel between missions and jobs.
Use a WAiNK map for the last stragglers until the count reads 100.
tips: Each spot counts once, so a map is the fastest way to finish.
Do WAiNK stops in batches by district to avoid criss-crossing the map.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges and the trophy pops. Challenges are the game's small feats — driving, shooting, flying, exploration and the rest — and they complete in the background as you play. Fifty is a modest count against the full list, so most players get this one without trying, just by playing widely: drive fast, shoot straight, explore, and the challenges tick off one by one.
steps: Play widely: drive, shoot, fly and explore across Leonida.
Check the challenge list to see which ones are close to done.
The trophy pops when the fiftieth challenge completes.
tips: Challenges complete in the background — no special mode is needed.
The challenge list shows your nearest completions; chase those first.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then escape, and the trophy pops. First build the heat: commit crimes with your partner beside you until the wanted level hits 4 stars. Then break line of sight, get out of the search area, and stay hidden until the stars clear. The partner must be with you for the whole escape — if they get busted or left behind, it does not count.
steps: Bring your partner along and commit crimes until the wanted level hits 4 stars.
Break line of sight and leave the search area with your partner.
Stay hidden until the stars clear; the trophy pops on escape.
tips: Alleyways and the metro hide you faster than open roads.
Keep your partner close — if they are left behind, the attempt fails.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner, keeping your wanted level the whole time, and the trophy pops. The trick is the opposite of the usual getaway: you must keep the heat on. Rob the first shop, then drive straight to the second and third without losing the cops — do not hide, do not wait for the stars to clear. Pick three shops close together, plan the route in advance, and keep moving.
steps: Pick three shops close together and plan the route.
Rob the first shop with your partner, then drive straight to the second.
Rob the third without ever losing the wanted level; the trophy pops.
tips: Shops close together matter — a long drive gives the cops time to lose you.
Keep moving between shops; hiding clears the wanted level and voids the run.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles and the trophy pops. A vehicle counts as discovered the first time you drive it, and Leonida is full of different cars, bikes, boats and aircraft. The counter climbs as you travel, so vary your rides: steal different cars, try bikes, take boats, and fly when you can. The vehicle list shows which types you have found and which are still missing.
steps: Drive a different vehicle every time you travel.
Try bikes, boats and aircraft as well as cars.
The trophy pops when the hundredth distinct vehicle is discovered.
tips: The vehicle list shows what is still missing — chase the rare types.
Car meets and docks are good places to find vehicles you have not driven.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus and the trophy pops. Combat Focus is the slow-motion aiming mode — trigger it when a group of enemies is close together, then work through them one by one before the meter runs out. A gang shootout or a police standoff with enemies bunched up is the right moment. An automatic weapon with a big magazine helps, since reloading wastes the focus window.
steps: Find a spot where 5 or more enemies are bunched together.
Trigger Combat Focus and take them down one by one.
Five downs inside one focus window pops the trophy.
tips: An automatic weapon with a big magazine suits this best.
Wait for enemies to bunch up before triggering focus — do not waste it on singles.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport and the trophy pops. Head to VCIA, get yourself a plane, and take off without filing a flight — no ticket, no schedule, just throttle up and leave. The runway is the obvious spot, but any long straight stretch of tarmac works if you can build speed. Expect airport security to notice, so be quick about it.
steps: Go to VCIA and find a plane on the tarmac.
Get in, throttle up and take off without a schedule.
The trophy pops as you leave the airport airspace.
tips: A small plane is easier to steal and lift than a big one.
Security will chase you — get airborne fast and climb away.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: This one is about the Rhino tanks: get into a Rhino and survive the heat that follows. Rhinos appear at the military base and in high-wanted-level responses, so either steal one from the base or push your wanted level up until the army rolls in. Once you are in the driver's seat, the trophy is about the ride — drive it, use it, and stay alive while the whole map comes after you.
steps: Find a Rhino at the military base or by raising your wanted level.
Get in the driver's seat and drive it.
Survive the response; the trophy pops from the ride.
tips: The military base is the reliable place to find a Rhino.
A Rhino is slow to steal but nearly unstoppable once you are in.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected and the trophy pops. This is a stealth job: go in quiet, avoid the cameras and the staff's line of sight, take the goods, and leave before anyone raises the alarm. Night helps, and so does a silenced weapon for the cases that need breaking. If the alarm goes off, leave and try again — a detected robbery does not count.
steps: Pick a jewelry store and case it first: cameras, staff, exits.
Go in quiet at night, avoid sight lines, and take the goods.
Leave before the alarm; the trophy pops on a clean getaway.
tips: Night and a silenced weapon make the quiet approach far easier.
If the alarm sounds, leave and retry — a detected run does not count.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape, and this silver trophy pops. Each bank vault is a planned job: get in, crack the vault, grab the cash, and get out ahead of the police response. The vaults are spread across Leonida, and each one counts once — five different vaults, five clean escapes. Bring heavy weapons, full armour, and a fast getaway car for each one, and do not linger after the cash is in the bag.
steps: Find a bank vault, plan the entry and the getaway car.
Crack the vault, grab the cash and escape the police.
Repeat at four more vaults; the trophy pops on the fifth escape.
tips: Five different vaults count — repeats of the same vault do not.
Leave the moment the cash is bagged; lingering brings the heavy response.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape, and the trophy pops. Armored trucks run set routes around Leonida — spot one, stop it, and crack it open. Blocking the road works, as does ramming it to a stop; once it is still, break the rear doors and take the cash. Then lose the wanted level that follows. A sticky bomb on the doors is the classic opener, and a fast car is the classic exit.
steps: Find an armored truck on its route and stop it.
Break the rear doors and take the cash.
Escape the wanted level; the trophy pops on the getaway.
tips: Block the road ahead of the truck rather than chasing it from behind.
Sticky bombs open the rear doors fast — then grab and go.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida and the trophy pops. An area counts as explored when you have driven or walked through it, and the map shades in what you have covered. Work district by district: Vice City first, then the beaches, the swamps, the farmland and the small towns, until the whole map is shaded. The map screen shows which areas are still dark.
steps: Open the map and note which areas are still unexplored.
Drive through each dark area until it shades in.
The trophy pops when all 52 areas are explored.
tips: Work district by district instead of criss-crossing the map.
Boats and planes reach the areas roads do not.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs and the trophy pops. Each gang runs its own operations around Leonida — stash houses, labs, drops — and you need one hit on each gang's turf. Learn which gang holds which area, hit their operation, take the goods, and get out before their backup arrives. Nine gangs, nine hits, and the trophy follows the last one.
steps: Learn which gang holds each area of the map.
Rob one illegal operation on each gang's turf.
The trophy pops on the ninth gang's operation.
tips: Gang backup arrives fast, so grab and go — do not linger.
One hit per gang counts; repeats on the same gang do not.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach and the trophy pops. Head to a bar on Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and take it in with the ocean in front of you. It is a quiet moment trophy — no chase, no shootout, just a drink and a view. Sunset makes it better, but any time of day counts as long as you are at the beach with a cocktail in hand.
steps: Go to a bar on Ocean Beach.
Order a cocktail and enjoy it with the ocean view.
The trophy pops once the moment registers.
tips: Any bar on Ocean Beach works — pick the one with the best view.
Sunset is the prettiest time, but the trophy counts any time of day.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style and the trophy pops. Pick a vehicle showroom, get in a car inside it, and drive straight out through the glass — the classic GTA exit. Speed matters: build up inside the showroom if you can, or just floor it from the door. The mess is the point, so do not worry about the damage.
steps: Go to a vehicle showroom and get in a car inside.
Drive straight out through the glass frontage.
The trophy pops on the smash exit.
tips: Build speed inside the showroom if the floor allows it.
Any showroom with a glass front works — pick the biggest one.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley and the trophy pops. Go to the alley, pick up a ball, and bowl a proper game — the follow-through is the key, so let the swing finish instead of cutting it short. You do not need a strike or a high score; a full, clean follow-through on your delivery is what the game reads.
steps: Go to the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
Pick up a ball and bowl with a full follow-through.
The trophy pops on the completed delivery.
tips: Let the swing finish — a cut-short delivery does not count.
No high score is needed; the follow-through is the trigger.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: This is the partnership moment: do something with your partner that draws a crowd, and the trophy pops. The exact trigger is a shared feat with mass appeal — a stunt, a show or a public moment done together. Play with your partner, look for the moments the game flags as crowd-pleasers, and the trophy follows the one that lands.
steps: Play with your partner and look for crowd-pleasing moments.
Pull off a shared feat with mass appeal.
The trophy pops when the moment lands.
tips: Partner moments flag on screen — watch for the game's reaction.
Big public stunts with your partner are the likeliest triggers.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices and the trophy pops once PlayStation's count reaches 500. The game tracks the choices you make — dialogue picks, mission decisions, the small calls and the big ones — and the counter climbs across the whole playthrough. There is nothing special to do beyond playing and choosing: pick dialogue options, take decisions in missions, and the count reaches 500 on its own in a full playthrough.
steps: Play the story and side content, making choices as they come.
Pick dialogue options and mission decisions instead of skipping them.
The trophy pops when the count reaches 500.
tips: Choices count across the whole game, so do not skip dialogue.
Side strands are full of choices — they add up fast.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.unconfirmed_note: The exact trigger is not yet pinned down. The best current reading is that it pops on succeeding at something on the second try; treat this guide as a lead, not a certainty.
trophies.guide: This trophy is labelled unconfirmed: its exact trigger is not yet pinned down, and this guide will not pretend otherwise. The description — 'Second time's the charm' — points at succeeding at something on the second attempt, so the best current reading is to fail something once and then succeed at it right away. If that does not pop it, keep playing: the trigger will be confirmed by the community, and this guide will be updated when it is.
steps: Fail an activity or challenge once, then succeed at it on the immediate second try.
If it does not pop, keep playing and watch for community confirmation.
Do not grind blindly — wait for the confirmed trigger.
tips: Unconfirmed means unconfirmed: do not waste hours on a guessed trigger.
Check PowerPyx and PSNProfiles for updates on this one.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange and the trophy pops. Leonida hides odd sights — a strange encounter, an unexplained event, something that makes you stop and stare. The description's 'What the hell just happened?' is the clue: it pops when you see one of the game's weird moments. Explore the odd corners of the map, especially at night, and let the strange find you.
steps: Explore Leonida's odd corners, especially at night.
Watch for strange encounters and unexplained events.
The trophy pops when you witness one.
tips: Remote spots and late hours are where the strange things happen.
If a moment feels weird, stay and watch it play out.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.unconfirmed_note: The exact trigger is not yet pinned down. The best current reading is knocking someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle; treat this guide as a lead, not a certainty.
trophies.guide: This trophy is labelled unconfirmed: its exact trigger is not yet pinned down, and this guide will not pretend otherwise. The description — 'Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by' — points at knocking someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle, like bowling pins. The best current reading is to drive past a pedestrian and land a melee hit from the car. If that does not pop it, wait for community confirmation rather than grinding blindly.
steps: Get in a car and find a pedestrian on a quiet street.
Drive past and land a melee hit from the moving vehicle.
If it does not pop, wait for the confirmed trigger.
tips: Unconfirmed means unconfirmed: do not waste hours on a guessed trigger.
Check PowerPyx and PSNProfiles for updates on this one.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts and the trophy pops. Marked Bills come from the bigger robberies, and your contacts will clean them for a cut — the laundered total is what counts, so keep feeding bills through until the counter reads $250,000. Do the robbery set first so the bills are already in hand, then launder in batches.
steps: Collect Marked Bills from robberies and heists.
Launder them through your contacts in batches.
The trophy pops when the laundered total reaches $250,000.
tips: Do the robbery set first so the bills are already in hand.
Laundering takes a cut, so the gross take needs to be well over $250,000.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops and the trophy pops. Every shop in Leonida counts — clothes, weapons, food, car parts — and the total is cumulative across the whole game. By the late game you will have spent a good part of it just by gearing up; top it off with a shopping run for the things you actually want, like a good car and a full wardrobe.
steps: Buy what you need as you play: weapons, armour, clothes, car parts.
Check the spent total in the stats screen.
Top it off with a shopping run until the total reads $100,000.
tips: Weapons and cars are the fastest way to reach the total.
The total is cumulative across the whole game, so it builds on its own.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties and the trophy pops. Garages are bought from the property listings around Leonida, and each one gives you storage for your cars. They are not cheap, so save this for the late game when cash is plentiful — after the heists and the laundering, 8 garages is an easy buy. The property menu shows which ones you already own.
steps: Save up until cash is plentiful, late in the game.
Buy garages from the property listings around Leonida.
The trophy pops when the eighth garage is purchased.
tips: Garages are a late-game buy — do not stretch for them early.
The property menu shows which garages you already own.
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app and the trophy pops. The Scooter Bros app is the delivery-side app on your phone: register a vehicle to it and it becomes available for the app's jobs. Any 10 vehicles count, so use the cars you already own and drive — register each one in the app, one at a time, until the counter reads 10.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app on your phone.
Register a vehicle you own to the app.
Repeat with nine more vehicles; the trophy pops on the tenth.
tips: Any 10 vehicles count — use the ones you already drive.
Register them one at a time and watch the counter climb.
